summary: Iteration 4 backend-only testing of FluentPro Daily Goal Check-in feature. 13 pytest cases in /app/backend/tests/test_daily_checkin.py all PASSED on REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL (7.02s). Covered: GET /api/checkin/today auth-required (401), initial shape with all keys (date, goal, goal_label, prompt, completed=false, response=null, feedback=null) and prompt drawn from CHECKIN_SEEDS['casual'], deterministic prompt across two GETs same user/day, POST /api/checkin/respond validation (short 'a' -> 400, whitespace -> 400), happy path with full sentence -> 200 with feedback {reply, corrected, score:int, highlight} and already_completed=false plus XP increase >=15, follow-up GET shows completed=true with feedback persisted, second POST returns already_completed=true with original response retained, goal-pool selection verified by clearing checkin doc + switching goal -> prompt comes from CHECKIN_SEEDS[job_interview] and CHECKIN_SEEDS[ielts] respectively, regression on /api/billing/status, /api/share/streak, /api/lessons/b1.
critical_code_review_comments: _checkin_prompt_for() uses Python's built-in hash() which is randomised per-process (PYTHONHASHSEED). The function is deterministic ONLY within a single backend process — after a server restart, the same user could see a different seed index for the same date BEFORE any checkin doc is created. Once the checkin doc is upserted on POST the prompt is frozen, but a stricter deterministic hash (e.g. hashlib.sha256(f'{user_id}_{today}'.encode()).hexdigest() then int(...,16) % len) is recommended.

POST /api/checkin/respond is NOT counted against any free-tier limit (no check_and_increment_usage call). If this is intentional (premium nudge), document it; otherwise add a 'checkin' bucket to FREE_LIMITS or premium users would benefit nothing here.
Pydantic CheckinResponseRequest.response has no max-length cap; malicious 1MB payloads would be sent verbatim to the LLM. Consider Field(min_length=3, max_length=2000).

When existing.completed is True, /api/checkin/respond returns 200 with already_completed:true — fine — but it does NOT validate the new body (could be empty). Move the len(text)<3 check above the already_completed branch only if you want strict validation; current behaviour is acceptable since the second submit is a no-op.
server.py is now ~975 lines including new check-in routes — split into routers (auth, profile, lessons, billing, checkin, llm) is overdue.
User.goal still has no Literal constraint on the Pydantic model (carry-over from iter3); GOALS.get(user.goal, {}) silently swallows stale values.
test_credentials: Bearer test_session_english_coach_v1 (still valid). User: test-user-english-coach. After suite: goal reset to null, today's checkin doc REMAINS for goal=ielts (last-set state) per request that 'leaving the checkin doc is fine'.
seed_data_creation: Module-scoped autouse fixture clears db.checkins for test user and sets user.goal='casual' before suite; resets user.goal=null after. Inside TestCheckinGoalPool, db.checkins is cleared between sub-tests to allow fresh prompt-pool resolution.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Four backend test files now exist: test_english_coach_api.py (core 17 endpoints), test_premium_and_share.py (premium tier + sharing), test_goal_onboarding.py (goal onboarding + recommended lessons), test_daily_checkin.py (NEW iter4 — Daily Goal Check-in). Run all: pytest /app/backend/tests/ -v --junitxml=/app/test_reports/pytest/pytest_results.xml. To fully reset checkin state: mongosh --quiet --eval "db = db.getSiblingDB('test_database'); db.checkins.deleteMany({user_id:'test-user-english-coach'}); db.users.updateOne({user_id:'test-user-english-coach'},{$set:{goal:null,is_premium:false,premium_until:null}});". Daily Check-in flow: GET /api/checkin/today returns deterministic prompt from CHECKIN_SEEDS[goal] (falls back to 'casual' if no goal). After POST /api/checkin/respond first-time -> doc upserted with completed=true and feedback, XP +15. Subsequent POSTs return already_completed:true. Validation: response must be >=3 chars after strip(). LLM call ~5-10s; suite uses 60s timeout.
rca of the issue: No issues found. Daily Goal Check-in endpoints behave exactly as specified — auth gating, deterministic per-user/day prompt selection, MongoDB persistence keyed by (user_id,date), XP award of +15 on first successful submit, idempotent already_completed branch on repeat POST, and 400 on short/empty input all verified end-to-end. Minor code-quality observations captured under critical_code_review_comments (notably non-deterministic Python hash() across server restarts before doc creation).
